header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Kaplan (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aurora Head of IT), Liam O'Neill (Aurora Security Architect), Dr. Priya Rao (Aurora VP Clinical Ops)
summary: POC scoping for Private networking and data residency. Customer requires VPC peering/PrivateLink options, strict EU data residency for some datasets, egress constraints and auditability. Discussed POC goals (latency/throughput targets), benchmarking plan, timeline (2-3 week POC + prep), and next steps including security docs and network setup.
topics: Regions and data residency (EU vs US)
POC success criteria: latency, throughput, quality
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Sophie, AE on the account, and with me is Ravi, our SE who will run the bench.
[00:12] Maya: Hi all, this is Maya. We wanted to dig into the private networking and data residency aspects before we greenlight the POC.
[00:20] Ravi: Great, quick agenda: confirm success criteria, size the workload, agree benchmark queries, and lay out networking steps - VPC peering vs PrivateLink and any egress rules.
[00:28] Liam: From security side, we need to make sure traffic doesn't traverse public internet for PHI queries, and that logs are kept in EU for certain datasets. Also looking for explicit egress constraints and cost implications.
[00:40] Sophie: Totally. Our Private offering supports cross-account VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your preference. Peering is straightforward if you want full network access; PrivateLink gives more managed endpoints and avoids route table changes.
[00:55] Maya: Are there latency differences between the two? For our clinical triage flow we need p95 under 600ms for 2k token chat sessions.
[01:06] Ravi: In practice PrivateLink adds a small hop, usually 20-50ms depending on region. The bigger latency levers are model size and KV cache hits; with our Dedicated nodes and prefix caching we'd expect to meet p95 ~400-500ms for 2k-token interactive sessions in-region.
[01:22] Priya: When you say Dedicated nodes, does data ever leave our VPC? Our compliance team insists certain PHI never exits EU.
[01:30] Sophie: For Redwood Private we can deploy control plane in your account or in our private tenancy with region-specific nodes. For EU-only data we can pin the model to EU regions and ensure KV/cache and logs are kept in-region; we will not mirror PHI to US unless you opt in.
[01:43] Liam: We also need to control egress to third-party telemetry. Can you disable outbound calls from the runtime?
[01:49] Ravi: Yes, outbound egress is configurable. We can lock down security groups and NAT rules. Our audit logs and traces can be pushed to your CloudWatch/Splunk collector in-region.
[02:00] Maya: Ok, sounds promising. For the POC itself, what throughput should we size for? We'll run synthetic traffic and a subset of real queries. Expecting bursty traffic around 50 concurrent sessions up to 200 requests/minute.
[02:15] Ravi: Good to know. For a safety margin we'd propose a single Dedicated pod with 4 GPUs for the POC if you're using a 7B-ish open model; that supports ~80-120 concurrent smaller chat sessions. If you want to test 2k-token sessions consistently we may recommend 8 GPUs.
[02:30] Sophie: Pricing estimate we'll include in the follow-up, but for the POC we can offer a short reserved capacity with defined hours to avoid surprise egress charges.
[02:40] Liam: On data residency, we have two classes: Class A (PHI) must remain in EU region and logs retained 7 years on-prem-like retention; Class B (de-identified) can go to US.
[02:52] Priya: Success criteria from clinical side: 1) accuracy within our benchmark prompts (we'll share a set), 2) p95 latency below 600ms for interactive triage, 3) no PHI leaves EU, 4) audit logs show request-level metadata and model version.
[03:08] Ravi: Perfect. For benchmarking we'll need your prompt set and representative token lengths. We'll run three passes: cold start, warmed cache, and high-concurrency to measure p95/p99 and cost.
[03:20] Sophie: Timeline thought: week 1 - network setup and security onboarding (peering/PrivateLink, IAM roles), week 2 - bench runs and tuning, week 3 - review and iterate. So roughly a 2-3 week POC.
[03:33] Maya: We can commit to that timeline if network prep is quick. Who sets up the peering?
[03:37] Ravi: We can create the endpoint in our account and guide your infra team to accept peering, or we can do a cross-account PrivateLink service. For peering you'll need to update route tables and security groups; for PrivateLink we'll provide an endpoint service name and you attach an ENI in your subnet.
[03:54] Liam: We prefer PrivateLink for least blast radius, but we need to validate cross-account IAM and also that egress stay in-region. Can you provide a checklist?
[04:02] Sophie: Yes, we'll send a PrivateLink checklist and a VPC peering runbook. Also the SOC2 whitepaper and encryption/KMS integration guide.
[04:10] Priya: What about model updates and rollouts? We need model version pinned for the POC so outputs are deterministic between runs.
[04:17] Ravi: You can pin model versions and we support rollbacks. For the bench we'll pin to a specific model sha we provide. We'll also expose version metadata in every response so you have request-level traceability.
[04:29] Maya: Can you log the prompt but redact PHI automatically?
[04:34] Sophie: We offer configurable redaction hooks; typically we recommend sending raw prompts to your private logging pipeline where you can apply your own DLP. If you want automatic redaction, we can show options but we typically avoid doing PHI redaction on our side for compliance reasons.
[04:48] Liam: Egress costs are a concern. If we peer in the same region there shouldn't be cross-az charges except inter-AZ. If data goes to a different region there are inter-region egress fees.
[04:58] Ravi: Right, we'll ensure the POC deploys into your EU region (e.g., eu-west-1). We'll measure data egress during bench runs and include that in the cost analysis.
[05:08] Sophie: For the benchmark we'd like to run three profile loads: 1) low-concurrency interactive (50 concurrent), 2) sustained throughput (200 requests/min), 3) spike test (500 req/min for 5 min). We'll capture latency percentiles and token cost.
[05:22] Maya: We'll prepare the prompt set. Also need a pre-approved list of stakeholders to see logs.
[05:27] Priya: One more question: can we run the runtime on-prem if we need full air-gap for some customers?
[05:33] Ravi: Yes, Private on-prem packaging is possible but it increases setup time. For this POC it's easier to do VPC in your cloud account. On-prem would be a separate scoping with our infra team.
[05:43] Sophie: Any blockers to schedule the bench the week of Feb 22?
[05:46] Maya: That's fine, we'll confirm by Feb 17 after we get the runbook and internal approvals.
[05:52] Liam: On auditing, we need request-level logs with model version, timestamp, source IP, and a hashed user id. Can you surface hashed IDs?
[05:59] Ravi: Yes, we can include hashed identifiers in logs and stream to your SIEM.
[06:06] Sophie: Ok let's recap next steps... (recap).
[06:10] Sophie: We'll send PrivateLink checklist, SOC2 + KMS docs, draft pricing for the POC, and benchmarking script. You'll confirm prompt set and egress constraints.
[06:20] Maya: Good. Thanks everyone.
[06:22] Priya: Thanks.
[06:24] Liam: Thanks, speak soon.
[06:26] Sophie: Bye.

[NOTE] Transcript has occasional transcription artifacts; product names might appear slightly different (e.g., Redwood Dedicated/Redwood PrivateLink).
